headword: {日雇|ひやと}い{労働者|ろうどうしゃ}
reading: ひやといろうどうしゃ

definitions.explanation: A worker hired on a day-to-day basis rather than under a long-term contract, typically paid at the end of each day's work.

examples.japanese: {日雇|ひやと}い{労働者|ろうどうしゃ}として{働|はたら}く。
examples.english: to work as a day laborer.

examples.japanese: {現場|げんば}には{多|おお}くの{日雇|ひやと}い{労働者|ろうどうしゃ}がいた。
examples.english: There were many day laborers at the work site.

examples.japanese: {不況|ふきょう}のときは、{日雇|ひやと}い{労働者|ろうどうしゃ}が{仕事|しごと}を{見|み}つけるのは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: In a recession, it is hard for day laborers to find work.

notes:
Composed of {日雇|ひやと}い ('daily hiring') + {労働者|ろうどうしゃ} ('worker'). Refers to workers engaged by the day, common in construction and manual labor.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {日雇|ひやと}い{労働|ろうどう}: day labor
- {日雇|ひやと}いで{働|はたら}く: to work by the day

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {派遣|はけん}{社員|しゃいん}: dispatch/temp worker — employed through an agency, usually longer term
- {正社員|せいしゃいん}: full-time regular employee — the contrasting status
